To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Taiwanese fishing industry has been growing steadily since 1959.

(a) energy use in Taiwan's commercial marine fishery has increased by 10-fold over the past five decades; (b) the ratio of emissions to production has increased by almost 50% over the same period; and (c) the Taiwanese fishing fleet is likely to become more energy-efficient and less polluting in the future.
the Taiwanese fishing sector is energy-intensive, and that energy use and pollutant emissions are likely to continue to rise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy consumption of Taiwanese fishing fleets, and the associated emissions of greenhouse gases and air pollutants.
the implications of energy use for the Taiwanese fishing fleet.
the energy use and emissions from the Taiwanese commercial marine fishery and the implications of these for future development of the sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a need for the government to implement a policy of sustainable fisheries development, and to encourage fishing vessel owners to invest in cleaner and more energy-efficient fishing vessels, gear and equipment.

the Taiwanese fishing industry is a major contributor of atmospheric pollutants and GHG emissions, and that there is a need to implement a more effective and sustainable fishing management policy to reduce the environmental impact of the industry.
energy efficiency and environmental impact of the fishing fleet have been improved in the past decade, but there is room for further improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy consumption of Taiwanese fishing vessels has increased significantly, and that this increase is likely to continue.
the energy efficiency and the pollution intensity of fishing vessels in Taiwan have improved, but not to the degree that is required to meet the challenges of sustainable fishing practices.
the fishing sector is a significant contributor to energy use and atmospheric pollution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fishing fleet is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and atmospheric pollutants, and it should be a target for mitigation policies.
energy efficiency of fishing vessels is a key component of sustainable fisheries management.
the Taiwanese government has a responsibility to implement policies to reduce the energy intensity of its marine fisheries and to reduce emissions to the atmosphere.
